chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq, from Saʿdān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, the heart has two ears. So when the servant intends a sin, the spirit of faith says to him, “Do not do it,” and the Satan says to him, “Do it.” And when he is upon its belly, the spirit of faith is removed from him.

key_terms.أُذُنَيْنِ: two ears, symbolizing receptivity to opposing inner influences
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: the Satan, who urges the servant toward disobedience
key_terms.الْقَلْبِ: the heart, understood as the inner faculty of moral and spiritual perception
key_terms.بِذَنْبٍ: to a sin, meaning an act of disobedience
key_terms.رُوحُ الْإِيمَانِ: the spirit of faith, the inner force calling one away from sin
key_terms.نُزِعَ: was removed, indicating withdrawal of spiritual support

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about how the heart responds to temptation and sin?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the heart is a place of inner moral conflict, receiving opposing calls from the spirit of iman and from the Satan. It highlights the spiritual danger of moving toward sin, indicating that persistent advance into sin leads to the removal of the spirit of iman.
